mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate indicates tighter monetary policy, which may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, negatively impacting the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate suggests a strong labor market, which may boost consumer confidence and increase corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates expanding economic activity, which may lead to increased demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST exceeds 2000, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests increased economic output, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO exceeds 120, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales and housing starts indicates strong demand, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when both RSAFS and HOUST increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth indicates a strong economy, which may lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 grows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in employment and a decrease in unemployment rate suggests a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index suggests inflationary pressures, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 200, the hypothesis is rejected.
